findings.summary: B-12's report-level half is unasserted: no test reads the architect UNPARSEABLE case's report.json entry to show it carries actual.outcome "UNPARSEABLE" and no error key.
findings.evidence: `Select-String -Path src/*.test.ts -Pattern 'B-12'` finds exactly one test, `src/eval-compare.test.ts:143` ("B-12 projects a guardian review's outcome, and UNPARSEABLE as a value"). It asserts `projectOutput(guardian, unparseable)` equals `{ outcome: "UNPARSEABLE" }` and that `compareProjection({outcome:"SHIP"}, {outcome:"UNPARSEABLE"})` is "MISMATCH". No test in src/eval-command.test.ts dispatches a guardian case whose stub writes an unparseable review, so no assertion ever reads a report.json entry for that case. `pnpm vitest run src/eval-command.test.ts` (21 passed) contains no `pm`/`architect` MISMATCH scenario at all.
findings.expected: acceptance-manifest.json B-12 observableResult: "a unit test asserts the pm projection, and asserts the architect case entry in report.json has outcome MISMATCH with actual.outcome \"UNPARSEABLE\" and no error key".
findings.observed: The two composed halves (projection, then comparison) are asserted separately at the unit level; the composed end-to-end claim — that a full `runEvalCli` run records this case as MISMATCH rather than ERROR in report.json, with no `error` key — is not asserted anywhere. The behavior is correct on inspection (`src/eval-command.ts:236-242` attaches `actual` and omits `error` on any non-MATCH compare result, and `src/eval-report.ts:83-84` serializes by presence), so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect: a future change that routed an UNPARSEABLE projection through `failed()` in `src/eval-command.ts:214` would leave every existing test green.
findings.clearCondition: A test named for B-12 dispatches a guardian case through runEvalCli whose stub writes an unparseable review against an expected SHIP, and asserts that case's report.json entry has outcome "MISMATCH", actual.outcome "UNPARSEABLE", and no "error" own key.
